title: SSC MTS — English Language | Narration
description: Subject-wise test on Narration (English Language) for SSC MTS. 20Q.
subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the given sentence: She said to me, “Do not waste your time.”

options.text: She forbade me not to waste my time
options.explanation: The verb 'forbade' is too strong and changes the meaning.

options.text: She advised me not to waste my time
options.explanation: Correctly uses 'advised' for a negative imperative.

options.text: She told me not to waste my time
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, 'told' does not convey the nuance of advice.

options.text: She ordered me do not waste my time
options.explanation: Incorrect structure and verb usage.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb ‘said to’ changes to ‘advised’ in indirect speech when the imperative is negative. The structure becomes ‘advised + object + not + infinitive’.
questions.hint: Identify the correct reporting verb change for negative imperatives.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Identify the correct transformation of the following into indirect speech: He said, “I have finished my work.”

options.text: He said that he had finished his work
options.explanation: Correct tense transformation.

options.text: He said that he has finished his work
options.explanation: Tense remains in present perfect, which is incorrect.

options.text: He said that he finished his work
options.explanation: Tense changes to simple past, which is incorrect.

options.text: He said that he was finishing his work
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and meaning.

questions.explanation: The present perfect tense ‘have finished’ changes to past perfect ‘had finished’ in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past.
questions.hint: Remember the tense change for present perfect to past perfect.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Which option correctly converts the following into indirect speech? She said, “I will help you tomorrow.”

options.text: She said that she would help me the next day
options.explanation: Correct tense and time adverb transformation.

options.text: She said that she will help me tomorrow
options.explanation: Tense and time adverb remain unchanged, which is incorrect.

options.text: She said that she would help me tomorrow
options.explanation: Correct tense but incorrect time adverb.

options.text: She said that she will help me the next day
options.explanation: Incorrect tense but correct time adverb.

questions.explanation: The future tense ‘will help’ changes to ‘would help’ and ‘tomorrow’ changes to ‘the next day’ in indirect speech.
questions.hint: Apply the correct changes for future tense and time adverbs.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for: “I have been living here since 2010,” she said.

options.text: She said that she was living there since 2010
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and word 'since' should remain.

options.text: She said that she had been living there since 2010
options.explanation: Correct tense and word transformation.

options.text: She said that she has been living there since 2010
options.explanation: Tense remains in present perfect continuous, which is incorrect.

options.text: She said that she had lived there since 2010
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous ‘have been living’ changes to past perfect continuous ‘had been living’ in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past.
questions.hint: Remember the tense change for present perfect continuous to past perfect continuous.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Which option correctly changes the following into indirect speech? “You should consult a doctor,” he told me.

options.text: He told me that I should consult a doctor
options.explanation: Correct modal verb usage.

options.text: He told me that I shall consult a doctor
options.explanation: Incorrect modal verb change.

options.text: He told me that I must consult a doctor
options.explanation: Incorrect modal verb change.

options.text: He told me that I could consult a doctor
options.explanation: Incorrect modal verb change.

questions.explanation: The modal ‘should’ remains unchanged in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past.
questions.hint: Modal verbs like 'should' do not change in indirect speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the given sentence: “He said to me, ‘Don’t touch that wire — it’s live!’”

options.text: He warned me not to touch that wire as it was live
options.explanation: Correct reporting verb and tense change.

options.text: He told me not to touch that wire because it is live
options.explanation: Incorrect tense for 'is live'.

options.text: He said to me not to touch that wire since it was live
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb and tense.

options.text: He advised me don’t touch that wire as it is live
options.explanation: Incorrect structure and tense.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb ‘said to’ changes to ‘warned’ to convey caution. The exclamation mark is replaced by ‘as’ or ‘since’ to show reason.
questions.hint: Identify the correct reporting verb change to convey caution.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Identify the correct indirect speech for: “I can swim across the river,” he said.

options.text: He said that he could swim across the river
options.explanation: Correct modal verb change.

options.text: He said that he can swim across the river
options.explanation: Modal verb remains unchanged, which is incorrect.

options.text: He said that he might swim across the river
options.explanation: Incorrect modal verb change.

options.text: He said that he would swim across the river
options.explanation: Incorrect modal verb change.

questions.explanation: The modal ‘can’ changes to ‘could’ in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past.
questions.hint: Remember the modal verb change from 'can' to 'could'.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Which option correctly transforms the following into indirect speech? “The teacher said, ‘The Earth revolves around the Sun.’”

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun
options.explanation: Correct tense usage for universal truth.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth is revolving around the Sun
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

questions.explanation: When stating a universal truth, the tense does not change in reported speech.
questions.hint: Universal truths remain in the same tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the given sentence: “She said, ‘I have been working on this project for two months.’”

options.text: She said that she had been working on that project for two months
options.explanation: Correct tense and pronoun transformation.

options.text: She said that she was working on that project for two months
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

options.text: She said that she has been working on that project for two months
options.explanation: Tense remains in present perfect continuous, which is incorrect.

options.text: She said that she had worked on that project for two months
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous ‘have been working’ changes to past perfect continuous ‘had been working’ in reported speech.
questions.hint: Remember the tense change for present perfect continuous to past perfect continuous.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Which option correctly converts the following into indirect speech? “He said, ‘I will have completed the assignment by Monday.’”

options.text: He said that he would have completed the assignment by Monday
options.explanation: Correct tense and time reference transformation.

options.text: He said that he will have completed the assignment by Monday
options.explanation: Tense remains in future perfect, which is incorrect.

options.text: He said that he will complete the assignment by Monday
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

options.text: He said that he had completed the assignment by Monday
options.explanation: Incorrect tense change.

questions.explanation: The future perfect tense ‘will have completed’ changes to ‘would have completed’ in reported speech, and the time reference ‘Monday’ remains unchanged.
questions.hint: Apply the correct change for future perfect tense to conditional perfect tense.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the given sentence: The teacher said, 'The earth moves around the sun.'

options.text: The teacher said that the earth moved around the sun.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense changes unnecessarily for universal truths.

options.text: The teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.
options.explanation: Correct because the present simple tense is retained for universal truths.

options.text: The teacher says that the earth moves around the sun.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the reporting verb is in the present tense, not past.

options.text: The teacher had said that the earth moves around the sun.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'had said' unnecessarily shifts the tense.

questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past tense and the reported speech expresses a universal truth, the tense of the reported speech does not change.
questions.hint: Universal truths retain their tense in reported speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect form of the sentence: She said to me, 'I have finished my work.'?

options.text: She told me that I had finished my work.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the pronoun 'I' should refer to the original speaker, not the listener.

options.text: She told me that she had finished her work.
options.explanation: Correct because the pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' and 'my' to 'her' to match the reporting context.

options.text: She told me that she had finished her work.
options.explanation: Same as option B, but listed again due to duplication in the original text.

options.text: She told me that I have finished my work.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should shift to past perfect in reported speech.

questions.explanation: In reported speech, first and second person pronouns change according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
questions.hint: Pronouns must align with the reporting subject and object.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form of the sentence: He said, 'Alas! I have failed.'

options.text: He exclaimed with joy that he had failed.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'Alas' indicates sorrow, not joy.

options.text: He exclaimed with sorrow that he had failed.
options.explanation: Correct because 'Alas' is replaced with 'exclaimed with sorrow.'

options.text: He said that alas he had failed.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'alas' is not used in reported speech; emotions must be conveyed explicitly.

options.text: He cried that he has failed.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'cried' does not convey the meaning of 'Alas' and the tense is wrong.

questions.explanation: 'Alas' indicates sorrow, so the correct transformation uses 'exclaimed with sorrow.'
questions.hint: The word 'Alas' denotes sorrow.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect form of the sentence: The teacher said, 'Sit down, students.'?

options.text: The teacher ordered the students to sit down.
options.explanation: Correct because the imperative is reported as an order.

options.text: The teacher requested the students to sit down.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'requested' does not convey the authoritative nature of the original command.

options.text: The teacher ordered the students to sit down.
options.explanation: Same as option A, but listed again due to duplication in the original text.

options.text: The teacher told the students to sit down.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'told' is less authoritative than 'ordered' in this context.

questions.explanation: The imperative 'Sit down' in direct speech is usually reported as an order.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in direct speech are often reported as orders.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the sentence: He said, 'I shall go as soon as it is possible.'

options.text: He said that he would go as soon as it was possible.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'would' is used for polite requests or hypotheticals, not future intention.

options.text: He said that he should go as soon as it was possible.
options.explanation: Correct because 'shall' in the first person changes to 'should' in reported speech for future intention.

options.text: He said that he will go as soon as it was possible.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should shift to past for reported speech.

options.text: He said that he shall go as soon as it was possible.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'shall' does not change to 'shall' in reported speech.

questions.explanation: 'Shall' in the first person changes to 'should' in reported speech when expressing future intention.
questions.hint: First-person 'shall' changes to 'should' in reported speech for future intention.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect form of the sentence: She said, 'I have been reading this book for two hours.'?

options.text: She said that she had read that book for two hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the continuous aspect is lost.

options.text: She said that she had been reading that book for two hours.
options.explanation: Correct because the present perfect continuous tense shifts to past perfect continuous.

options.text: She said that she was reading that book for two hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the perfect aspect is lost.

options.text: She said that she read that book for two hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect because both the tense and aspect are wrong.

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous tense in direct speech changes to past perfect continuous in reported speech.
questions.hint: Present perfect continuous tense shifts to past perfect continuous in reported speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the sentence: He said, 'I bought a car yesterday.'

options.text: He said that he had bought a car the previous day.
options.explanation: Correct because 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day' and the tense shifts to past perfect.

options.text: He said that he had bought a car the day before.
options.explanation: Correct because 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before' and the tense shifts to past perfect.

options.text: He said that he bought a car the previous day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense does not shift to past perfect.

options.text: He said that he has bought a car the day before.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense is wrong and 'the day before' is used instead of 'the previous day'.

questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' changes to 'the previous day' and the tense shifts to past perfect.
questions.hint: Time adverbs and tenses must shift in reported speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect form of the sentence: The officer said, 'Bring the documents immediately.'?

options.text: The officer requested to bring the documents immediately.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'requested' does not convey the authoritative nature of the command.

options.text: The officer asked if he could bring the documents immediately.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the imperative is changed to a question, which alters the meaning.

options.text: The officer ordered to bring the documents immediately.
options.explanation: Correct because the imperative is reported as an order in an authoritative context.

options.text: The officer told to bring the documents immediately.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'told' is less authoritative than 'ordered' in this context.

questions.explanation: The imperative 'Bring' in direct speech is reported as an order when the context suggests authority.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences with authoritative context are reported as orders.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the sentence: She said, 'Let us go for a picnic.'

options.text: She suggested that they should go for a picnic.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'should' is unnecessary; the infinitive form is preferred.

options.text: She proposed that they would go for a picnic.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'would' is not the correct modal for proposals.

options.text: She suggested going for a picnic.
options.explanation: Correct because 'Let us' is reported as a suggestion using the gerund form.

options.text: She proposed that they go for a picnic.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'that they go' is subjunctive and not the most natural form.

questions.explanation: 'Let us' in direct speech is usually reported as a suggestion or proposal.
questions.hint: 'Let us' is reported using 'suggest' or 'propose' in indirect speech.
questions.subject: mts-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect form of the sentence: He said, 'What a beautiful day it is!'?

options.text: He said that it was a beautiful day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the exclamatory nature is lost.

options.text: He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful day.
options.explanation: Correct because the exclamatory sentence is reported using 'exclaimed that' and the tense shifts to past.

options.text: He said that it is a very beautiful day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense does not shift to past.

options.text: He exclaimed that it is a very beautiful day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense does not shift to past.

questions.explanation: 'What a beautiful day!' is an exclamatory sentence, so it is reported using 'exclaimed that' and the tense shifts to past.
questions.hint: Exclamatory sentences are reported using 'exclaimed that' and tense shifts to past.
questions.subject: mts-english
